To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of education in Mexico's public primary schools is very unequal and that this inequality is related to the social origin of students and to the socioeconomic context of schools, as well as the internal functioning of the school.

(1) the quality of the education provided in public primary schools in the state of Puebla varies greatly; (2) the quality of education in schools is related to the socioeconomic status of their students and to the quality of the teaching staff; (3) the quality of teaching staff varies greatly among schools and is related to the quality of education provided; (4) the quality of schools' infrastructure varies greatly among schools, and is not directly related to the quality provided; and (5
there is a significant relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and educational quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the problem of equity in the distribution of educational quality in primary education in Mexico.

the problem of the quality of education and the inequality of its distribution in Mexico, and more specifically with the question of how the quality of education is distributed in different social contexts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of primary education is distributed unequally in Mexico.
the quality of education in Mexico is determined by the socioeconomic conditions of the students' families.
the quality of education in the schools in the five socioeconomic zones is different, and that the quality of the education is related to the socioeconomic zone where the school is located.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found evidence that there are important differences in quality of education between schools located in different social contexts, and that these differences are not only due to the socioeconomic status of families, but to other factors related to the educational system itself.
the quality of education in primary schools varies according to the socio-economic status of the community where the school is located.
we are trying to answer the question: How can we explain the different quality levels in the education system, and what can be done to improve the quality of education for all?
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the fact that the educational system is highly stratified, it is possible to find schools with similar quality levels, regardless of their location.
the educational system has not been able to overcome the effects of the socioeconomic context in the distribution of educational quality.

there is a significant gap in the quality of the education provided to children in Mexico, which is not only a function of the socio-economic conditions of the children, but is also a result of the quality of the school itself.
